children: Malaysia's 2027 budget is likely to incorporate a mix measures to stimulate domestic demand, catalyze investment and capitalize on external growth opportunities, TA Securities analyst Kaladher Govindan says. Malaysia's GDP growth is expected to come in at 4.6% in 2027, down from an estimated 5.1% in 2026 but still resilient. Govindan sees tailwinds from robust domestic activity and export demand, including AI-driven growth in shipments of electronic and firmer energy shipments. Inflation is expected to remain manageable at 1.7% in 2027. It stands at 1.8% so far this year. Against that backdrop, he sees scope for Bank Negara to raise the policy rate by 25 bps to 3.00% as resilient employment, wage growth and healthy household balance sheets mean tighter financial conditions won't materially dampen demand. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
